summary: Rauchtown fire tower, Clinton County PA: steel tower built 1935 by CCC labor, removed 1973; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1973, per the register. No source describes what remains at the site today.

events.note: Erected by CCC workers from Pine Camp (CCC Camp 127); April 1935 notice says 80 feet tall. The register dates the steel I-S tower to 1935.
Frank Aumiller of Jersey Shore appointed towerman for the new tower and went on duty for the spring fire season.
A 1955 item describes an 85-foot tower about five miles from Rauchtown, maintained by Ralph Rauch. It does not say whether this is the same structure as the state tower.
Register says the tower was removed in 1973.
Registered September 16, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The February 1935 notice says Catfish Mountain, about 2 1/2 miles south of Rauchtown. The April 1935 notice says the summit of Kalbfleish Mountain, three miles south. The register coordinates are kept as recorded; they were not checked against either name.

The register and 1935 notices give 80 feet (24.4 m), which the record keeps. A 1955 item describes an 85-foot tower maintained by Ralph Rauch about five miles away. It is not clear that it is the same tower.

sources.title: Rauchtown - Forest Lookouts (1935 and 1955 newspaper transcriptions)

notes_for_editor: Only two sources. The register and 1935 notices agree on the build date and height, and the register gives the 1973 removal. No source describes the site today, and no source says whether it is public. A Wikipedia entry for Rauchtown does not mention the tower. The anyplaceamerica tower page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The 1955 85-foot tower may be a different structure; the record keeps 24.4 m. Mountain name conflicts (Catfish vs Kalbfleish) are unresolved. Record material is null; the register and 1935 notices both say steel, so material could be added. No photos.
